method: Same-agent English/Marathi close reading and reverse paraphrase; not independent or human review.
scope: All fourteen translated content blocks on equinumerosity, its equivalence properties, preservation of enumerability and two exercises.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Frege's plate-and-knife example compares finite size by a one-to-one spatial correspondence without counting.
samples.checks: Both coverage directions, uniqueness and the frozen citation remain present.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A and B are equinumerous exactly when a bijection A→B exists; equinumerosity is reflexive, symmetric and transitive.
samples.checks: Identity, inverse and composition witnesses and all cardeq formulas are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: If A and B are equinumerous, then A is enumerable exactly when B is enumerable.
samples.checks: Both directions and the inverse-bijection reversal are retained.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Under the included definition, the empty case transfers through f:A→B, while in the nonempty case composing a PosInt-surjection onto A with f gives a PosInt-surjection onto B.
samples.checks: The conditional branch, quantified surjectivity witness and displayed composition equation remain exact; OLSIZ-008 corrects the two g/f name errors.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The alternative branch composes bijections whose domain is Nat or a finite initial segment; the exercises preserve equinumerosity under disjoint unions and identify every infinite enumerable set with Nat.
samples.checks: Both conditional branches, domain alternatives, disjointness hypotheses and conclusions remain unchanged; OLSIZ-009 records the source wording inconsistency.

limitations: T058's equinumerosity vocabulary remains open to specialist correction.
No independent linguistic certification has been performed.
